subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Laboratory thermometers are used to measure the temperature of the human body.
There is no method to convert temperature from one heat scale to another.
The normal human body temperature is 45°C.
The normal human body temperature is 98.6°F.

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**The normal human body temperature:**

 
• The normal human body temperature is universally recognized to be approximately 98.6°F, which is equivalent to 37°C. This value is considered the average temperature for a healthy human being. However, variations in body temperature can occur due to factors such as age, activity, time of day, and individual physiological differences.
 
• Human body temperature is measured using thermometers, typically in degrees Fahrenheit or Celsius. The value of 98.6°F (37°C) represents the oral temperature, which is measured under the tongue. It is important to note that body temperature may vary slightly depending on the method of measurement (oral, rectal, axillary, or tympanic), the time of the day, and the external environment.
